transcript.text: Good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining today's pre-authorization review. As we all know, we have a student research team proposing an online survey of first-year students about their transition to college, and before I can give final authorization and record the operating conditions, I need to hear from each of you. Let's go through the key elements of the draft proposal: it describes an anonymous survey, indefinite retention of responses, an open invitation to all first-year students, and eligibility for a public research presentation. I'd like to hear from the research coordinator, the privacy officer, and the faculty mentor about any conditions you believe should be included before we authorize this survey to launch. Who would like to start?

transcript.text: I'd like to start. During my testing of the survey platform, I confirmed that it collects respondent email addresses by default. This is a critical issue for a survey that's supposed to be anonymous. Before launch, two things must happen: the email collection feature must be disabled in the launch settings, and the existing test responses — which contain email addresses — must be deleted before any student data are gathered. I recorded this in the platform test log, which is kept separate from the draft proposal, so it wouldn't have been visible to the rest of you.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Thank you, Elias. I'd like to share what I found during my policy review. The survey includes questions about mental-health treatment and immigration status, which are classified as sensitive student data. Because of this, the project requires three specific conditions: first, explicit written consent from respondents; second, encrypted institutional storage of the responses; and third, deletion of all research responses exactly 30 days after collection closes. I entered this determination in the privacy review system, which is separate from the research proposal, so it wouldn't have been visible to the rest of you. These conditions need to be added before authorization is granted.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: Thank you, both. I need to share what I've documented in the faculty mentoring record, which hasn't yet been attached to the proposal. I confirmed that the course attached to this project awards credit only for a study capped at exactly 100 enrolled respondents, and it permits dissemination only at the closed university undergraduate symposium — not at a public presentation. These are hard course conditions, so two operating conditions need to be added: the survey must be capped at exactly 100 enrolled respondents, and the presentation venue must be changed from a public research presentation to the closed university undergraduate symposium.
